The High Line.text: This park used to be a freight rail line. You just walked a piece of the West Side the trains left behind, instead of letting a map skip over it.

Inwood Hill Park.text: This is the last natural forest on Manhattan. People who only follow a pin never learn it is up here.

Staten Island Ferry Terminal.text: The ferry is free, and it is how Manhattan actually reaches Staten Island. The chompers have to wait on the dock. You do not.

Brooklyn Bridge.text: You can cross the East River on foot. That walk is the original link between these boroughs, and a transit app usually hides it.

Little Island.text: A public park now stands in the river where the old piers were. The city keeps adding places you can only understand by going there.

The Battery.text: This lawn is the bottom of the island. Once you have stood here, the shape of Manhattan is yours, not just a subway diagram.

Katz's Delicatessen.text: Houston Street has been slicing pastrami since 1888. Knowing a city means knowing a counter on a side street, not only the skyline.

Sheep Meadow.text: A flock grazed this field until 1934. You found it by the streets, which is how a mental map gets built.

ferry.text: This boat is the fast way to Staten Island. It is public transit, and the hunters cannot board.

Brooklyn Bridge.text: You are walking the crossing yourself. A map turns this into a line you never feel under your feet.
